verdicts.note: Tested against 10,000 sets of arbitrary levels on one-minute dollar-mark, yen and pound quotes (1996-98), support and resistance levels published by six FX firms stopped intraday trends 60.8% of the time against 56.2% for arbitrary levels: a real but modest edge in a narrow setting, for firms' published levels rather than Fibonacci lines or fair value gaps as such, with the firms' own strength ratings not meaningful and trading profits left untested.

Measuring thousands of algorithmically detected trend corrections in S&P 100 and Eurostoxx 50 stocks (1989-2016), the authors find retracement depths follow a continuous distribution with no level of great statistical significance, even in a fine 0.01-bin histogram: pullbacks do not cluster at Fibonacci ratios, though this working paper covers only Fibonacci (not fair value gaps), daily stock data, and uses histograms rather than a formal test against random levels.
